title: Arms Sales Notification
items_summary: Non-MDE additions (aircraft components, parts, accessories; training; logistics and program support) for RQ-4 Global Hawk sustainment under original Transmittal 19-48 (Contractor Logistics Support and related services for RQ-4 Block 30 remotely piloted aircraft).
summary: This is a Section 36(b)(5)(C) enhancement report for the Republic of Korea, amending the July 29, 2019 notification (Transmittal 19-48) for RQ-4 Global Hawk support. It adds $399 million in non-MDE items, raising the total estimated case value from $950 million to $1.349 billion, and notes that the MDE value remains $0.472 million (three Kearfott INS/GPS units added in 2022). The notice states the additions increase capability and will help Korea sustain its RQ-4 Block 30 fleet and advance interoperability with U.S. forces. The highest classification level is SECRET.

DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE

Office of the Secretary

[Transmittal No. 26-1J]


Arms Sales Notification

AGENCY: Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA), Department of 
Defense (DoD).

ACTION: Arms sales notice.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The DoD (referred to herein as ``the Department,'' 
``Department of War'' or ``DoW'') is publishing the unclassified text 
of an arms sales notification.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Urooj Zahra at (703) 695-6233, 
[email protected], or [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This 36(b) arms sales notification is 
published to fulfill the requirements of section 155 of Public Law 104-
164 dated July 21, 1996. The following is a copy of the attached 
Transmittal 26-1J.

    Dated: November 17, 2026.
Stephanie J. Bost,
Alternate OSD Federal Register Liaison Officer, Department of Defense.
Transmittal No. 26-1J

REPORT OF ENHANCEMENT OR UPGRADE OF SENSITIVITY OF TECHNOLOGY OR 
CAPABILITY (SEC. 36(B)(5)(C), AECA)

    (i) Prospective Purchaser: Republic of Korea
    (ii) Sec. 36(b)(1), AECA Transmittal No.: 19-48
    Date: July 29, 2019
    Implementing Agency: Air Force
    (iii) Description: On July 29, 2019, Congress was notified by 
congressional certification transmittal number 19-48 of the possible 
sale, under Section 36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act, of 
Contractor Logistics Support; program management; training for pilots 
maintenance, logistics and communications personnel; depot and 
organizational level maintenance; minor modifications and upgrades; 
spares and repair/return parts; operational flight support; program 
analysis; publications and technical documentation; U.S. Government and 
contractor technical and logistics services; and other related elements 
of logistics and program support for RQ-4 Global Hawks. The estimated 
total cost was $950 million. There was no Major Defense Equipment (MDE) 
associated with this sale.
    On July 15, 2022, Congress was notified by congressional 
certification transmittal number 0K-22 of the possible sale, under 
section 36(b)(5)(A) of the Arms Export Control Act of the addition of 
the following MDE items: three (3) Kearfott Inertial Navigation System/
Global Positioning System units. The estimated total value of the MDE 
items was $0.472 million. The total estimated case value remained $950 
million.
    This transmittal notifies the inclusion of the following non-MDE 
items: aircraft components, parts, and accessories; personnel training 
and training equipment; and other related elements of logistics and 
program support. The estimated total value of the new items is $399 
million. No additional MDE items will be added and will remain at 
$0.472 million. The estimated total case value will increase by $399 
million to a revised $1.349 billion.

[[Page 75306]]

    (iv) Significance: This notification accounts for requested 
additional non-MDE items not included in the original notification. The 
inclusion of this non-MDE represents an increase in capability over 
what was previously notified. The proposed articles and services will 
support the Republic of Korea to sustain and operate its fleet of RQ-4 
Block 30 remotely piloted aircraft and will significantly advance U.S. 
interoperability with the Republic of Korea's armed forces.
    (v) Justification: The proposed sale will support the foreign 
policy and national security of the United States by improving the 
security of a major ally that is an important force for political 
stability and economic progress in the Indo-Pacific region.
    (vi) Sensitivity of Technology:
    The Sensitivity of Technology statement contained in the original 
notification applies to items reported here.
    The highest level of classification of defense articles, 
components, and services included in this potential sale is SECRET.
    (vii) Date Report Delivered to Congress: September 24, 2026.
